newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle calls mixed, feeders higher.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle calls mixed, feeders higher.

text.p: Early calls on CME live cattle futures ranged from 0.100 cent per lb lower to 0.100 higher while feeder cattle were called 0.100 to 0.300 cent higher, livestock analysts said.

Indications were mixed on live cattle with nearbys expected to be weighed down by a mostly easier tone to cash beef. Weekend retail beef clearance was not as good as hoped for, possibly due to cold weather in some areas, which will weigh on sentiment, analysts said.
However, deferred months may show a firmer tone on expected gains in feeder cattle, they said.
The April contract expires on Wednesday and trade may also be choppy in the month, they said.
Feeder cattle futures were seen showing carryover strength following a runup in the latest CME feeder cattle index as expected.
The latest CME feeder cattle index jumped $1.12 higher to $71.97 per cwt, the highest price level in over two years since February 23, 1995.
Expectations of lower corn futures should also provide strength, they added.
